# Vitis Utility Library

Vitis Utility Library is an open-sourced Vitis library of common patterns of streaming and storage access.
It aims to assist developers to efficiently access memory in DDR, HBM or URAM, and perform data distribution, collection,
reordering, insertion, and discarding along stream-based transfer.

Check the [comprehensive HTML document](https://docs.xilinx.com/r/en-US/Vitis_Libraries/utils/index.html) for more details.

## Requirements

### Software Platform

Supported operating systems are RHEL8.10, RHEL9.2,RHEL9.3,RHEL9.4,RHEL9.5 and Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS, 22.04.4 LTS, 22.04.5 LTS.

And C++14 should be enabled during compilation.

### Development Tools

This library is designed to work with Vitis 2022.2 and later,
and a matching version of XRT should be installed.

## Source Files and Application Development
Vitis libraries are organized into L1, L2, and L3 folders, each relating to a different stage of application development.

**L1**:
      Makefiles and sources in L1 facilitate HLS based flow for quick checks. Tasks at this level include:

* Check the functionality of an individual kernel (C-simulation)
* Estimate resource usage, latency, etc. (Synthesis)
* Run cycle accurate simulations (Co-simulation)
* Package as IP and get final resource utilization/timing details (Export RTL)
       
	**Note**:  Once RTL (or XO file after packaging IP) is generated, the Vivado flow is invoked for XCLBIN file generation if required.

**L2**: Makefiles and sources in L2 facilitate building XCLBIN file from various sources (HDL, HLS or XO files) of kernels with host code written in OpenCL/XRT framework targeting a device. This flow supports:

* Software emulation to check the functionality
* Hardware emulation to check RTL level simulation
* Build and test on hardware

## Design Flows

The common tool and library pre-requisites that apply across all design flows are documented in the requirements section above.

Recommended design flow is shown as follows:


### Shell Environment

Setup the build environment using the Vitis script, and set the installation folder of platform files via `PLATFORM_REPO_PATHS` variable.

```console
source /opt/xilinx/2025.2/Vitis/settings64.sh
export PLATFORM_REPO_PATHS=/opt/xilinx/platforms
```

Setting the `PLATFORM_REPO_PATHS` to installation folder of platform files can enable makefiles in this library to use the `PLATFORM` variable as a pattern.
Otherwise, full path to .xpfm file needs to be provided through the `PLATFORM` variable.

### Running HLS cases

L1 provides the modules to work distribution and result collection in different algorithms, manipulate streams:
including combination, duplication, synchronization, and shuffle, updates URAM array in tighter initiation internal (II).

The recommend flow to evaluate and test L1 components is described as follows using Vivado HLS tool.
A top level C/C++ testbench (typically `algorithm_name.cpp`) prepares the input data, passes them to the design under test,
then performs any output data post processing and validation checks.

A Makefile is used to drive this flow with `make run TARGET=<TARGET> PLATFORM=<PLATFORM>`

`TARGET` can be any of the following values:

- `csim` (high level simulation)
- `csynth` (high level synthesis to RTL)
- `cosim` (cosimulation between software testbench and generated RTL)
- `vivado_syn` (synthesis by Vivado)
- `vivado_impl` (implementation by Vivado)

The flow is launched from the shell by calling `make` with variables set as in the example below:

```console
    . /opt/xilinx/xrt/setup.sh
    export PLATFORM_REPO_PATHS=/opt/xilinx/platforms
    cd L1/tests/specific_algorithm/
    make run TARGET=csim  PLATFORM=u250_xdma_201830_1 # Only run C++ simulation on U250 card
```

To enable more than C++ simulation, just switch other steps to `1` in `make` command line.
The default value of all these control variables are ``0``, so they can be omitted from command line
if the corresponding step is not wanted.

As well as verifying functional correctness, the reports generated from this flow give an indication of logic utilization,
timing performance, latency and throughput.
The output files of interest can be located at the location of the test project where the path name is "test.prj".

1	# Vitis Vision Library
2	
3	The AMD Vitis™ Vision library is a set of 100+ kernels, optimized for AMD FPGAs, AI Engine, and SoCs, based on the OpenCV computer vision library. The kernels in the Vitis Vision library are optimized and supported in the Vitis Tool Suite.
4	
5	## Hardware and Software Requirements
6	
7	The Vitis Vision library is designed to work with Zynq™, Zynq Ultrascale+™, Versal™, and Alveo™ FPGAs. The library has been verified on zcu102, zcu104, vck190, U50, and U200 boards. AIE-ML functions are verified on VEK280 board.
8	
9	### Prerequisites
10	
11	* Valid installation of [Vitis™ 2026.1](https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/ug1742-vitis-release-notes/Installing-the-Vitis-Software-Platform) or later version and the corresponding licenses.
12	* Xilinx Runtime ([XRT](https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/ug1701-vitis-accelerated-embedded/Installing-Xilinx-Runtime-and-Platforms)) must be installed. XRT provides software interface to AMD FPGAs.
13	* Install [OpenCV-4.4.0]((https://github.com/opencv/opencv/tree/4.4.0)) x86 libraries (with compatible ``libjpeg.so``). x86 libs have to be used for:
14	
15	   a. L1 flow irrespective of target FPGA device being PCIe or embedded.
16	
17	   b. L2/L3 flow when the target device is PCIe based.
18	
19	    For L2/L3 flow targeting embedded platforms (for hardware emulation and hardware build), aarch32/aarch64 version OpenCV shipped within their *sysroot* should be used.
20	
21	* libOpenCL.so must be [installed](https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/ug1700-vitis-accelerated-data-center/OpenCL-Installable-Client-Driver-Loader) if not present.
22	* [Install the card](https://docs.xilinx.com/r/en-US/ug1301-getting-started-guide-alveo-accelerator-cards) for which the platform is supported in Vitis 2026.1 or later versions.
23	* If targeting an embedded platform, [install](https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/ug1701-vitis-accelerated-embedded/Installing-Embedded-Platforms) it and set up the [evaluation board](https://xilinx-wiki.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/A/pages/2712338433/Versal+AI+Edge+Series+VEK280+Evaluation+Kit).
24	
25	#### OpenCV Installation Guidance
26	
27	It is recommended to do a fresh installation of OpenCV 4.4.0 and not use existing libs of your system, as they may or may not work with the Vitis environment.
28	
29	**Please make sure you update and upgrade the packages and OS libraries of your system and
30	have cmake version>3.5 installed before proceeding.**
31	
32	The following steps can help install the basic libs required to compile and link the OpenCV calls in Vitis Vision host code.
33	
34	1. Create a directory "source" and clone [opencv-4.4.0](https://github.com/opencv/opencv/tree/4.4.0) into it.
35	2. Create a directory "source_contrib" and clone [opencv-4.4.0-contrib](https://github.com/opencv/opencv_contrib/tree/4.4.0) into it.
36	3. Create two directories: ``build`` and ``install``.
37	4. Open a bash terminal and *cd* to *build* directory
38	5. Run the command: ``export LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/``
39	6. Run the command: *cmake -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RELEASE
40	  -D CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=< path-to-install-directory>
41	  -D CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=< path-to-Vivado-directory-in-Vitis-installation>/tps/lnx64/gcc-6.2.0/bin/g++
42	  -D OPENCV_EXTRA_MODULES_PATH=< path-to-source_contrib-directory>/modules/
43	  -D WITH_V4L=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=OFF -DBUILD_ZLIB=ON
44	  -DBUILD_JPEG=ON -DWITH_JPEG=ON -DWITH_PNG=ON
45	  -DBUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF -DINSTALL_C_EXAMPLES=OFF
46	  -DINSTALL_PYTHON_EXAMPLES=OFF -DWITH_OPENEXR=OFF
47	  -DBUILD_OPENEXR=OFF < path-to-source-directory >*
48	7. Run the command: ``make all -j8``
49	8. Run the command: ``make install``
50	
51	The OpenCV includes and libs will be in the ``install`` directory
52	
53	## Source Files Organization
54	
55	The Vitis development environment supports a variety of build flows (based on the target (either AI Engine or Programmable Logic) and source type):
56	
57	* **PL [HLS/RTL]**: Kernels targeting FPGA (PL), coded in C/C++/HDL for Vitis HLS.
58	* **AIE**: Kernels targeting AI Engine programmed in C/C++ in accordance to AI Engine coding methodology.
59	* **PL+AIE**: Kernels that target both FPGA (PL) and AI Engine.
60	
61	To facilitate this, all unit level kernels are located in ``L1/include``. AI Engine kernels are located in ``L1/include/aie``.
62	
63	Examples and tests in L1, L2, and L3 will use these unit level kernels in various ways for building a project.
64	
65	The library is organized as follows:
66	
67	~~~
68	├── L1/
69	│   ├── README.md
70	│   ├── examples/
71	│   ├── include/
72	│   ├── lib/
73	│   └── tests/
74	├── L2/
75	│   ├── README.md
76	│   ├── examples/
77	│   └── tests/
78	├── L3/
79	│   ├── README.md
80	│   ├── benchmarks/
81	│   ├── examples/
82	│   └── tests/
83	├── data/
84	├── LICENSE.txt
85	├── README.md
86	├── docs/
87	│   ├── images/
88	│   ├── include/
89	│   ├── Makefile
90	│   ├── Makefile.sphinx
91	│   ├── rst files
92	│   ├── conf.py
93	│   ├── conf_bhp.py
94	│   ├── env.csh
95	├── ext/
96	│   └── xcl2/
97	└── library.json
98	~~~
99	
100	## Application Development
101	
102	The Vitis library is organized into L1, L2, and L3 folders to facilitate various development stages.
103	
104	**L1**:
105	      Makefiles and sources in ``L1/examples`` and ``L1/tests`` facilitate HLS-based flows for a quick check without considering the complexities of Platform, OpenCL/XRT, or framework. the following list shows the various uses:
106	
107	* Check the functionality of an individual kernel (C-simulation)
108	* Estimate resource usage, latency etc., (Synthesis)
109	* Run cycle-accurate simulation (Co-simulation)
110	* Package as IP, get final resource utilization/timing details (Export RTL)
111	       
112		**Note**:  When the RTL (or ``XO`` file after packaging IP) is generated, the Vivado flow can be invoked for ``XCLBIN`` file generation if required.
113	
114	**L2** :
115	       Makefiles and sources in ``L2/examples`` and ``L2/tests`` facilitate building XCLBIN file from various sources (HDL, HLS or XO files) of kernels with host code written in OpenCL/XRT frame work targeting a device.
116		   This flow supports:
117	
118	* Hardware emulation to check RTL level simulation
119	* Build and test on hardware
120	
121	For AI Engine development ``L1/include/aie-ml`` , ``L2/tests/aie-ml`` has sources and Makefiles executing the following tasks:
122	
123	* AIE simulation
124	* X86 simulation
125	* Hardware emulation
126	* Hardware build and run
127	
128	**L3** :
129	       Makefiles and sources in ``L3/examples`` and ``L3/tests`` demonstrate applications developed using multiple kernels in the pipeline. The Makefiles provided can be used for executing tasks same as L2.
130	
131	### Important
132	
133	* Vitis and OpenCV-4.4.0 x86 version libs need to be installed prior to the L1 flow. Other prerequisites are optional for the L1 flow.
134	
135	* Refer to the [L1 readme](https://github.com/Xilinx/Vitis_Libraries/blob/master/vision/L1/README.md) for details on how to setup the environment and run the L1 functions.
136

138

# Vitis Vision Library

The AMD Vitis™ Vision library is a set of 100+ kernels, optimized for AMD FPGAs, AI Engine, and SoCs, based on the OpenCV computer vision library. The kernels in the Vitis Vision library are optimized and supported in the Vitis Tool Suite.

## Hardware and Software Requirements

The Vitis Vision library is designed to work with Zynq™, Zynq Ultrascale+™, Versal™, and Alveo™ FPGAs. The library has been verified on zcu102, zcu104, vck190, U50, and U200 boards. AIE-ML functions are verified on VEK280 board.

### Prerequisites

* Valid installation of [Vitis™ 2026.1](https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/ug1742-vitis-release-notes/Installing-the-Vitis-Software-Platform) or later version and the corresponding licenses.
* Xilinx Runtime ([XRT](https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/ug1701-vitis-accelerated-embedded/Installing-Xilinx-Runtime-and-Platforms)) must be installed. XRT provides software interface to AMD FPGAs.
* Install [OpenCV-4.4.0]((https://github.com/opencv/opencv/tree/4.4.0)) x86 libraries (with compatible ``libjpeg.so``). x86 libs have to be used for:

   a. L1 flow irrespective of target FPGA device being PCIe or embedded.

   b. L2/L3 flow when the target device is PCIe based.

    For L2/L3 flow targeting embedded platforms (for hardware emulation and hardware build), aarch32/aarch64 version OpenCV shipped within their *sysroot* should be used.

* libOpenCL.so must be [installed](https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/ug1700-vitis-accelerated-data-center/OpenCL-Installable-Client-Driver-Loader) if not present.
* [Install the card](https://docs.xilinx.com/r/en-US/ug1301-getting-started-guide-alveo-accelerator-cards) for which the platform is supported in Vitis 2026.1 or later versions.
* If targeting an embedded platform, [install](https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/ug1701-vitis-accelerated-embedded/Installing-Embedded-Platforms) it and set up the [evaluation board](https://xilinx-wiki.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/A/pages/2712338433/Versal+AI+Edge+Series+VEK280+Evaluation+Kit).

#### OpenCV Installation Guidance

It is recommended to do a fresh installation of OpenCV 4.4.0 and not use existing libs of your system, as they may or may not work with the Vitis environment.

**Please make sure you update and upgrade the packages and OS libraries of your system and
have cmake version>3.5 installed before proceeding.**

The following steps can help install the basic libs required to compile and link the OpenCV calls in Vitis Vision host code.

1. Create a directory "source" and clone [opencv-4.4.0](https://github.com/opencv/opencv/tree/4.4.0) into it.
2. Create a directory "source_contrib" and clone [opencv-4.4.0-contrib](https://github.com/opencv/opencv_contrib/tree/4.4.0) into it.
3. Create two directories: ``build`` and ``install``.
4. Open a bash terminal and *cd* to *build* directory
5. Run the command: ``export LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/``
6. Run the command: *cmake -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RELEASE
  -D CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=< path-to-install-directory>
  -D CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=< path-to-Vivado-directory-in-Vitis-installation>/tps/lnx64/gcc-6.2.0/bin/g++
  -D OPENCV_EXTRA_MODULES_PATH=< path-to-source_contrib-directory>/modules/
  -D WITH_V4L=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=OFF -DBUILD_ZLIB=ON
  -DBUILD_JPEG=ON -DWITH_JPEG=ON -DWITH_PNG=ON
  -DBUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF -DINSTALL_C_EXAMPLES=OFF
  -DINSTALL_PYTHON_EXAMPLES=OFF -DWITH_OPENEXR=OFF
  -DBUILD_OPENEXR=OFF < path-to-source-directory >*
7. Run the command: ``make all -j8``
8. Run the command: ``make install``

The OpenCV includes and libs will be in the ``install`` directory

## Source Files Organization

The Vitis development environment supports a variety of build flows (based on the target (either AI Engine or Programmable Logic) and source type):

* **PL [HLS/RTL]**: Kernels targeting FPGA (PL), coded in C/C++/HDL for Vitis HLS.
* **AIE**: Kernels targeting AI Engine programmed in C/C++ in accordance to AI Engine coding methodology.
* **PL+AIE**: Kernels that target both FPGA (PL) and AI Engine.

To facilitate this, all unit level kernels are located in ``L1/include``. AI Engine kernels are located in ``L1/include/aie``.

Examples and tests in L1, L2, and L3 will use these unit level kernels in various ways for building a project.

The library is organized as follows:

~~~
├── L1/
│   ├── README.md
│   ├── examples/
│   ├── include/
│   ├── lib/
│   └── tests/
├── L2/
│   ├── README.md
│   ├── examples/
│   └── tests/
├── L3/
│   ├── README.md
│   ├── benchmarks/
│   ├── examples/
│   └── tests/
├── data/
├── LICENSE.txt
├── README.md
├── docs/
│   ├── images/
│   ├── include/
│   ├── Makefile
│   ├── Makefile.sphinx
│   ├── rst files
│   ├── conf.py
│   ├── conf_bhp.py
│   ├── env.csh
├── ext/
│   └── xcl2/
└── library.json
~~~

## Application Development

The Vitis library is organized into L1, L2, and L3 folders to facilitate various development stages.

**L1**:
      Makefiles and sources in ``L1/examples`` and ``L1/tests`` facilitate HLS-based flows for a quick check without considering the complexities of Platform, OpenCL/XRT, or framework. the following list shows the various uses:

* Check the functionality of an individual kernel (C-simulation)
* Estimate resource usage, latency etc., (Synthesis)
* Run cycle-accurate simulation (Co-simulation)
* Package as IP, get final resource utilization/timing details (Export RTL)
       
	**Note**:  When the RTL (or ``XO`` file after packaging IP) is generated, the Vivado flow can be invoked for ``XCLBIN`` file generation if required.

**L2** :
       Makefiles and sources in ``L2/examples`` and ``L2/tests`` facilitate building XCLBIN file from various sources (HDL, HLS or XO files) of kernels with host code written in OpenCL/XRT frame work targeting a device.
	   This flow supports:

* Hardware emulation to check RTL level simulation
* Build and test on hardware

For AI Engine development ``L1/include/aie-ml`` , ``L2/tests/aie-ml`` has sources and Makefiles executing the following tasks:

* AIE simulation
* X86 simulation
* Hardware emulation
* Hardware build and run

**L3** :
       Makefiles and sources in ``L3/examples`` and ``L3/tests`` demonstrate applications developed using multiple kernels in the pipeline. The Makefiles provided can be used for executing tasks same as L2.

### Important

* Vitis and OpenCV-4.4.0 x86 version libs need to be installed prior to the L1 flow. Other prerequisites are optional for the L1 flow.

* Refer to the [L1 readme](https://github.com/Xilinx/Vitis_Libraries/blob/master/vision/L1/README.md) for details on how to setup the environment and run the L1 functions.

* All the prerequisites need to be installed before starting with L2/L3 Vitis flow.

* For embedded devices, platforms and common images have to be downloaded separately from the [download center](https://www.xilinx.com/support/download/index.html/content/xilinx/en/downloadNav/embedded-platforms.html).

* Refer to [L2/L3 readme](https://github.com/Xilinx/Vitis_Libraries/blob/master/vision/L2/README.md) for details on how to setup the environment and run the L2/L3 functions.
	
* All limitations and constraints of Vitis ([OS support, compatibility](https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/ug1742-vitis-release-notes/Installation-Requirements) etc.) are also applicable to Vitis Vision library.



## Other Information

The user guides for Vitis Vision and using OpenCV on AMD devices are available [here](https://docs.xilinx.com/r/en-US/Vitis_Libraries/vision/index.html).

## Support

For questions and to get help on this project or your own projects, visit the [Xilinx Forums](https://support.xilinx.com/s/topic/0TO2E000000YKYAWA4/vitis-acceleration-acceleration?language=en_US)

## License and Contributing to the Repository

    You may obtain a copy of the License at

    WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
    See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
    limitations under the License.

To contribute to this project, follow the guidelines in the [Repository Contribution README][] (link yet to be updated)

## Acknowledgments

This library is written by developers at
- [AMD](http://www.xilinx.com)

## Changelog

**PL additions/enhancements:** :

    • New additions:
        • Preprocess-multidatatype
        • Layout Formatter        
        • Stitch
        • waitMat
        • Remap bicubic mode
        • AVFIRs L3 pipeline                
	
    • Updates:
        • Remap functionality updated to support different input and output sizes.
        • InitUndistorRectofyMapInverse function API updated to use float datatypes.
        • Fixed L2 isp-stats host side bug of x and y index swap.
        • Minor bugs and doc fixes
	
**AIE additions/enhancements:** :

**Known issues**

# Vitis Security Library

Vitis Security Library is an open-sourced Vitis library written in C++ for accelerating security applications in a variety of use cases.

It now covers one level of acceleration: the primitive level. In this level, it provides optimized hardware implementation of most common relational security algorithms.
Such as, Synmmetric Block Cipher, Symmetirc Stream Cipher, Asymmetric Cryptography, Cipher Modes of Operations, Message Authentication Code, and Hash Function.

Since all the primitive code is developed in HLS C++ with the permissive Apache 2.0 license,
advanced users can easily tailor, optimize or assemble property logic.
Benchmarks of 4 different acceleration applications are also provided with the library for easy on-boarding and comparison.

## Requirements

### Software Platform

This library is designed to work with Vitis 2022.2 and later, and therefore inherits the system requirements of Vitis and XRT.

Supported operating systems are RHEL8.10, RHEL9.2,RHEL9.3,RHEL9.4,RHEL9.5 and Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS, 22.04.4 LTS, 22.04.5 LTS.
And C++14 should be enabled during compilation.

### PCIE Accelerator Card

Hardware modules are designed to work with 16nm Alveo cards. Benchmarks are best tuned for U250, and could be tailored for other devices.
* [Alveo U200](https://www.xilinx.com/products/boards-and-kits/alveo/u200.html#gettingStarted)
* [Alveo U250](https://www.xilinx.com/products/boards-and-kits/alveo/u250.html#gettingStarted)
* [Alveo U280](https://www.xilinx.com/products/boards-and-kits/alveo/u280.html#gettingStarted)

### Shell Environment

Setup the build environment using the Vitis and XRT scripts:

```console
    $ source <install path>/2025.2/Vitis/settings64.sh
    $ source /opt/xilinx/xrt/setup.sh
```
## Source Files and Application Development
Vitis libraries are organized into L1, L2, and L3 folders, each relating to a different stage of application development.

**L1** :
      Makefiles and sources in L1 facilitate HLS based flow for quick checks. Tasks at this level include:

* Check the functionality of an individual kernel (C-simulation)
* Estimate resource usage, latency, etc. (Synthesis)
* Run cycle accurate simulations (Co-simulation)
* Package as IP and get final resource utilization/timing details (Export RTL)
       
	**Note**:  Once RTL (or XO file after packaging IP) is generated, the Vivado flow is invoked for XCLBIN file generation if required.

**L2** :
       Makefiles and sources in L2 facilitate building XCLBIN file from various sources (HDL, HLS or XO files) of kernels with host code written in OpenCL/XRT framework targeting a device. This flow supports:

* Software emulation to check the functionality
* Hardware emulation to check RTL level simulation
* Build and test on hardware

**L3** :
       Makefiles and sources in L3 demonstrate applications developed involving multiple kernels in pipeline. These Makefiles can be used for executing tasks, as with the L2 Makefiles.
       
## Design Flows

The common tool and library pre-requisites that apply across all design flows are documented in the requirements section above.

Recommended design flows are decribed as follows:

### L1

L1 provides the basic primitives which cover the most common algorithms in security.

The recommend flow to evaluate and test L1 components is described as follows using Vivado HLS tool.
A top level C/C++ testbench (typically `algorithm_name.cpp`) prepares the input data, passes them to the design under test, then performs any output data post processing and validation checks.


A Makefile is used to drive this flow with `make run TARGET=<TARGET> PLATFORM=<PLATFORM>`

`TARGET` can be any of the following values:

- `csim` (high level simulation)
- `csynth` (high level synthesis to RTL)
- `cosim` (cosimulation between software testbench and generated RTL)
- `vivado_syn` (synthesis by Vivado)
- `vivado_impl` (implementation by Vivado)

```console
	$ . /opt/xilinx/xrt/setup.sh
	$ export PLATFORM_REPO_PATHS=/opt/xilinx/platforms
	$ cd L1/tests/specific_algorithm/
	$ make run TARGET=csim PLATFORM=u250_xdma_201830_1 # Only run C++ simulation on U250 card
```


As well as verifying functional correctness, the reports generated from this flow give an indication of logic utilization, timing performance, latency and throughput. The output files of interest can be located at the location of the test project where the path name is correlated with the algorithm. i.e. the callable function within the design under test.

To run the Vitis projects for benchmark evaluation and test, you may need the example below:

```console
	$ ./opt/xilinx/xrt/setup.sh
	$ export PLATFORM_REPO_PATHS=/opt/xilinx/platforms
	$ cd L1/benchmarks/specific_algorithm/
	$ # Run hardware emulation for cycle-accurate simulation with the RTL-model
	$ make run TARGET=hw_emu DEIVCE=u250_xdma_201830_1
	$ # Run hardware to generate the desired xclbin binary
	$ make run TARGET=hw DEIVCE=u250_xdma_201830_1
	$ # Delete xclbin and host excutable program
	$ make cleanall
```

- **dependency.json**: inter-library dependencies.
- **platform_map.json**: maps logical platform names to actual .xpfm.

- **PL (Programmable Logic / FPGA)**: HLS C++ kernels synthesized to RTL, run on Alveo cards (U200/U250/U280/U50) or Zynq. Uses `v++` HLS flow.
- **AIE (AI Engine)**: on Versal devices (VCK190, VEK280, VEK385). C++ kernels in AIE graph (`adf::graph`), driven by `xrt::graph`. DSP, vision, solver have AIE kernels.

## Key data movement concept
- `hls::stream` + end-flag stream (`e_istrm`) is the universal data passing primitive between HLS kernels (utils library).

data.head: 629b2c979f65561f07e4e87b860f306cb480895e
data.rationale: 本仓库是 AMD Vitis 加速库的单体多库集合（9 个活跃库），核心抽象有三层：L1（HLS C++ 头件原语）/L2（内核+xclbin）/L3（多内核应用流水线），以及两条硬件路线：PL（FPGA/Alveo/Zynq，HLS→RTL）与 AIE（Versal AI Engine，ADF 图）。因此学习路径按"先共后分、先浅后深"组织：第 1-2 单元让读者从零认识项目定位、单仓库配置与 L1/L2/L3+PL/AIE 心智模型，并跑通第一个 HLS 用例；第 3-5 单元建立贯穿所有库的两个核心心智模型——HLS 流式内核模型与主机端 XRT/OpenCL 编程模型，以及 L2/L3 系统构建流程；第 6-11 单元按依赖与领域逐库深入（utils/data_mover 是底层，dsp/solver/blas 为数值计算，vision/security 为信号处理，motor_control/ultrasound 为垂直领域），每个库只用真实源码；第 12-15 单元进入专家层，覆盖性能与数据流架构、AIE 编程模型、测试与 CI 基础设施、二次开发与完整部署。讲义依赖关系沿"基础设施→机制→领域→进阶"递进，依赖图（utils←data_mover←dsp←solver）决定了领域库的讲解顺序。

units.title: 主机端编程：OpenCL 与原生 XRT

lectures.title: xcl2 OpenCL 主机辅助库
lectures.topic: 讲解 ext/xcl2 这个跨库共用的 OpenCL 主机辅助库：aligned_allocator 页对齐分配、find_binary_file 查找 xclbin、get_xil_devices 获取设备、is_emulation 判断仿真模式。
learning_goals: 理解 aligned_allocator 为何要页对齐
掌握 xclbin 的查找路径约定
学会用 xcl::get_xil_devices 枚举设备
lectures.practice_task: 写一段最小 OpenCL 主机代码，用 xcl::get_xil_devices() 找到设备并打印设备名，再说明 find_binary_file 会按哪些路径查找 xclbin。

lectures.title: 原生 XRT C++ API（xrt::device/kernel/bo/run）
lectures.topic: 以 dsp/L2 vss_fft_ifft_1d 的 host.cpp 为例，讲解现代原生 XRT C++ API：xrt::device、load_xclbin、xrt::kernel、xrt::run、set_arg/start/wait 的完整调用链。
learning_goals: 掌握 xrt::device 加载 xclbin 的流程
理解 xrt::kernel 与 xrt::run 的关系
学会用 set_arg/start/wait 驱动一次内核执行
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 host.cpp，按顺序列出主机加载 xclbin 后控制 mm2s/s2mm 内核的 API 调用序列，并解释 start()/wait() 的并发含义。

lectures.title: buffer object、同步与存储分区
lectures.topic: 讲解 xrt::bo 的创建、map 映射、sync 同步方向，以及 group_id 如何决定缓冲挂到哪个 DDR/HBM bank，从而影响带宽。
learning_goals: 理解 bo 的 map 与 sync 方向（to/from device）
掌握 group_id 与存储端口的对应关系
认识 DDR/HBM 多 bank 对带宽的意义
lectures.practice_task: 在 host.cpp 中定位 s2mm_bo 的创建与 sync 调用，说明为何要在读取结果前执行 XCL_BO_SYNC_BO_FROM_DEVICE，以及 group_id(0) 决定了什么。

units.title: 系统构建：L2/L3 流程

lectures.title: v++ L2 构建流程：XO→xsa→xclbin
lectures.topic: 以 example.mk 为例讲解 v++ -c 编译内核为 XO、v++ -l 链接为 xsa、再用 --package 生成 xclbin/SD 卡，以及 sw_emu/hw_emu/hw 三种 target 的区别。
learning_goals: 掌握 v++ -c/-l/--package 三段流程
理解 XO、xsa、xclbin 产物的关系
区分 sw_emu/hw_emu/hw 及其代价
lectures.practice_task: 对照 example.mk，列出从 XO 到能上板 xclbin 的三条 v++ 命令，并说明 system.cfg 在链接阶段的作用。

lectures.title: 数据搬运器与 DDR↔AIE 桥接
lectures.topic: 讲解 mm2s/s2mm PL 数据搬运内核如何把 DDR 数据变成流喂给 AIE/PL 内核，以及 data_mover 库提供的通用 4D 搬运器与 URAM 缓存。
learning_goals: 理解 mm2s/s2mm 在系统中的桥接角色
掌握 data_mover 库的 pl_data_mover/pl_4d_data_mover 用法
认识 URAM 缓存与 bi_dm 双向搬运
lectures.practice_task: 在 host.cpp 中找到 mm2s/s2mm 的内核名与连接关系，再从 data_mover 库选一个搬运器头件，描述它的模板参数如何控制维度与位宽。

lectures.title: 多内核流水线组合（L3）
lectures.topic: 讲解 L3 如何把多个内核串成应用流水线，以 vision L3 与 blas L3 GEMM 为例说明 examples/tests/benchmarks 的组织与构建。
learning_goals: 理解 L3 相对 L2 的组合价值
掌握多内核流水线的 host 控制方式
认识 L3 的 benchmarks 用途
lectures.practice_task: 浏览 vision/L3/examples 目录挑一个流水线示例（如 colordetect），描述它串联了哪些内核，并说明它与单个 L2 内核的区别。

units.title: DSP 库：从 HLS FFT 到 AIE 图

lectures.title: L1 HLS FFT（vitis_fft / 2dfft）
lectures.topic: 讲解 dsp L1 的 HLS FFT 实现：vitis_fft 与 vitis_2dfft 的目录结构、内核接口与对应 L1 测试（1dfft/2dfft/ssr_fft）。
learning_goals: 理解 dsp L1 HLS FFT 的组织
掌握 FFT 内核的流式接口与 SSR 概念
学会跑通一个 FFT L1 测试
lectures.practice_task: 进入 dsp/L1/tests/hw/1dfft 跑 csim，记录输入输出位宽与点数，并说明 SSR 如何影响并行度。

lectures.title: L2 AIE 内核全景（FFT/DDS/FIR/GeMM/排序/卷积）
lectures.topic: 系统介绍 dsp L1/include/aie 与 L2/tests/aie 下的 AIE 内核家族：mixed_radix_fft、dds_mixer、FIR 全家桶（sym/asym/hb/decimate/interpolate/resampler）、matrix_mult、bitonic_sort/merge_sort、conv_corr、cumsum、widget 等。
learning_goals: 掌握 dsp AIE 内核家族的类别
理解 traits/utils 三件式组织（kernel+traits+utils）
学会按 L2/tests/aie 找到对应测试
lectures.practice_task: 在 dsp/L2/tests/aie 下选一个内核（如 dds_mixer 或 matrix_mult），描述其目录与构建入口，并列出该内核的 traits 头文件里有哪些模板参数。

lectures.title: 端到端 AIE 示例：vss_fft_ifft_1d
lectures.topic: 以 vss_fft_ifft_1d 为完整案例，串起 AIE 图源码（aie.cpp/aie.hpp）、参数配置（my_params.cfg）、PL 搬运、主机控制与打包运行的全流程。
learning_goals: 理解一个完整 AIE 系统的文件构成
掌握 my_params.cfg 参数如何驱动代码生成
贯通 PL 搬运+AIE 图+主机控制的端到端流程
lectures.practice_task: 修改 my_params.cfg 里的 POINT_SIZE 或 SSR，按 example.mk 的说明重新生成 vss 并解释该参数对流的数量与图结构的影响。

units.title: Solver 库：矩阵分解与求解器

lectures.title: 稠密矩阵分解 HLS 内核
lectures.topic: 讲解 solver L1/include/hw 的 HLS 内核：Cholesky、LU、QR、SVD 分解与三角求解、矩阵求逆，以及对应的 L1 测试。
learning_goals: 掌握 solver 提供的矩阵分解种类
理解 Cholesky/QR 内核的接口与数据类型（含 cfloat 变体）
学会跑通一个分解 L1 测试
lectures.practice_task: 在 solver/L1 里找 cholesky 相关测试，跑 csim 并说明该内核对矩阵性质（如正定对称）的要求。

lectures.title: Solver AIE 内核与 L2 基准
lectures.topic: 讲解 solver 的 AIE 实现（aie 目录下 cholesky、qrd 等）以及 L2/benchmarks 如何在 Alveo 上评测分解与求解器性能。
learning_goals: 理解 solver 在 AIE 上的分解实现
掌握 qrd/cholesky 的 traits/utils 组织
学会用 L2/benchmarks 评测性能
lectures.practice_task: 浏览 solver/L2/benchmarks 选一个（如 gesvj），描述其构建与运行入口，并说明它与 L1 单内核测试在目标上的差别。

units.title: BLAS 库：三级抽象与 GEMM

lectures.title: BLAS 三级抽象与 GEMM
lectures.topic: 讲解 blas 库的 module/kernel/software-API 三级抽象、L1/include/hw 的 xf_blas 模块、L3 GEMM 软件接口，以及 run_test.py 测试总线的使用。
learning_goals: 理解 BLAS 的 module/kernel/API 三级定位
掌握 GEMM 从 L1 模块到 L3 API 的层级关系
学会用 run_test.py 驱动 blas 测试
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 run_test.py 与 blas_gen.mk，说明它们如何批量生成/运行 L1 测试，并指出 GEMM 在哪一级提供

units.title: Vision 库：OpenCV 加速与 AIE-ML

lectures.title: Vision 组织与 OpenCV 映射
lectures.topic: 讲解 vision 库的目录组织（core/imgproc/features/video/dnn + aie/aie-ml）、与 OpenCV 的 API 映射关系、对 OpenCV 4.4.0 的依赖与平台覆盖。
learning_goals: 理解 vision 的目录与功能域划分
掌握 vision 内核与 OpenCV 的对应关系
认识 PL/AIE/AIE-ML 三类内核的存放位置
lectures.practice_task: 在 vision/L1/include 里挑一个与 OpenCV 同名的内核（如 mean_stddev），对照说明 vision 版本的接口与数据类型差异。

lectures.title: PL 视觉内核与 L2 示例流程
lectures.topic: 讲解一个 PL 视觉内核从 L1 头件到 L2 examples/tests 的完整流程，包括 xcl2 主机与 hw_emu/hw 构建、OpenCV 输入输出处理。
learning_goals: 掌握 PL 视觉内核的 L1→L2 流程
理解 L2 examples 的 host + 内核 + makefile 组织
认识 OpenCV 图像作为输入输出的处理方式
minimal_modules: L1 内核到 L2 示例
lectures.practice_task: 在 vision/L2/examples 选一个示例（如 accumulate），列出其 host、内核源、makefile 三件，并说明输入图像如何加载到 bo。

lectures.title: AIE-ML 视觉函数与 L3 流水线
lectures.topic: 讲解 vision 的 AIE-ML 内核（L1/include/aie-ml 与 L2/tests/aie-ml）、其在 VEK280 上的仿真流程，以及 L3 多内核图像处理流水线。
learning_goals: 理解 AIE-ML 视觉内核的组织与定位
掌握 AIE 仿真/x86 仿真/hw_emu 流程
认识 L3 图像处理流水线
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 vision README 的 AIE 部分，说明 AIE-ML 函数在哪块板子验证，并挑一个 L3 流水线示例描述它串了哪些内核。

units.title: Security 库：密码学原语

lectures.title: 密码学原语目录与基准
lectures.topic: 讲解 security L1 提供的 HLS 密码学原语全家桶：对称（AES/DES/RC4/ChaCha20）、模式（CBC/CFB/CTR/ECB/GCM/CCM/XTS/OFB）、哈希（SHA/MD/BLAKE2b/Keccak/SHA3）、MAC（HMAC/GMAC）、非对称（RSA/DSA/EdDSA）与 VDF，以及 L1/benchmarks。
learning_goals: 掌握 security 原语的分类
理解 AES 各模式（如 aes256Gcm）的命名与组合方式
学会用 L1/benchmarks 评测加密吞吐
minimal_modules: 对称/非对称/哈希/MAC 分类
lectures.practice_task: 从 README 的函数表里选一个（如 aes256GcmEncrypt），在 xf_security 下找到其实现头件，并跑 L1/benchmarks 中一个（如 crc32）的 csim。

units.title: 领域专用：电机控制与超声

lectures.title: 电机控制：FOC/SVPWM/PWM_GEN/QEI
lectures.topic: 讲解 motor_control 库的 4 个 L1 算法 API（FOC、SVPWM_DUTY、PWM_GEN、QEI）、其 AXI 配置接口与 IPI 集成方式，以及 models_fp FP32 模型分支。
learning_goals: 理解 4 个电机控制 API 的职责与前后端关系（SVPWM_DUTY 前端 + PWM_GEN 后端）
掌握 AXI 配置接口与 IPI 集成
认识 models_fp 与 tests_fp32 的 FP32 精度测试
minimal_modules: AXI 接口与 FP32 模型
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 README，说明 SVPWM_DUTY 与 PWM_GEN 如何配合完成空间矢量调制，并指出 models_fp 相对默认实现的差异。

lectures.title: 超声波束合成器：L1→L2→L3 组合
lectures.topic: 讲解 ultrasound 库如何由 L1 向量/BLAS 运算（absV/mulMM/sumVV 等）组合出 L2 波束合成功能单元（kernel_apodization/delay/focusing/interpolation/sample），再构成 L3 完整 Beamformer（PW/SA/Scanline）。
learning_goals: 理解超声库的三层组合逻辑
掌握 L1 向量运算与 L2 kernel 的关系
认识 L3 完整 Beamformer 的三种模式
lectures.practice_task: 梳理 ultrasound L1/include 里 kernel_* 与底层向量运算（mulMM/sumVV 等）的依赖，画出 L1→L2 的组合关系图。

units.title: 性能与数据流架构

lectures.title: dataflow、SSR、datawidth 与 II 调优
lectures.topic: 从工程角度讲解 DATAFLOW 任务级流水、SSR（streaming split-radix）并行、datawidth 位宽取舍与 II 调优如何共同决定吞吐，结合 dsp/utils 真实内核。
learning_goals: 理解 DATAFLOW 与函数级并行的关系
掌握 SSR 如何线性扩展吞吐
学会用 datawidth 与 II 权衡面积/性能
lectures.practice_task: 以 my_params.cfg 的 SSR 参数为例，定量分析把 SSR 从 2 改到 4 对流的数量与理论吞吐的影响，并指出代价。

lectures.title: 资源/时序：URAM、HBM/DDR 分区与报告
lectures.topic: 讲解 URAM 数组与缓存（utils uram_array/cache）、DDR/HBM 多 bank 分区对带宽的影响，以及如何读综合/实现报告定位资源与时序瓶颈。
learning_goals: 理解 URAM 的使用场景与收益
掌握 DDR/HBM bank 分区对带宽的影响
学会从实现报告定位 II/时序/资源瓶颈
lectures.practice_task: 对比 utils/L1/tests 下 cache_ro_1DDR_with_e 与 cache_ro_2DDR_with_e 两个用例，说明双 DDR 如何提升只读缓存的带宽。

units.title: AIE 编程模型深入

lectures.title: ADF 图、窗口/流与 PL↔AIE 边界
lectures.topic: 讲解 ADF 图的构成（graph、kernel、连接）、窗口（window）与流（stream）两类数据交换、PL↔AIE 边界由 mm2s/s2mm 与 GMIO 桥接，结合 vss aie.hpp/aie.cpp。
learning_goals: 理解 ADF 图的 graph/kernel/connect 结构
区分 window 与 stream 两种 AIE 数据交换
掌握 PL↔AIE 边界的桥接方式
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 aie.hpp/aie.cpp，标出图中 PL 内核（mm2s/s2mm）与 AIE 内核的连接点，说明数据如何跨 PL↔AIE 边界。

lectures.title: AIE 图主机控制与 SD 卡打包
lectures.topic: 讲解用 xrt::graph 控制 AIE 图（reset/run/end）、system.cfg 连接描述、v++ --package 生成 SD 卡（rootfs/Image/launch 脚本）与 hw_emu 启动流程。
learning_goals: 掌握 xrt::graph 的 reset/run/end 控制
理解 system.cfg 的连接描述作用
学会用 v++ --package 生成 SD 卡并启动 hw_emu
lectures.practice_task: 对照 example.mk 的 example_sd_card/example_run 目标，解释 v++ --package 生成了哪些 SD 卡文件，以及 launch_hw_emu.sh 如何启动整个系统。

units.title: 测试、CI 与二次开发

lectures.title: 测试基础设施与 CI
lectures.topic: 讲解 L1 用例的 description.json（flow/platform_allowlist/topfunction/clock）、hls_config.tmpl/.cfg 生成、blas run_test.py 批量驱动，以及顶层 Jenkinsfile 如何串起各库 CI。
learning_goals: 理解 description.json 如何声明用例的流程与平台
掌握 hls_config 由模板生成的机制
认识 run_test.py 与 Jenkinsfile 的 CI 作用
lectures.practice_task: 为一个新的假想 L1 用例手写一份 description.json，指定 flow=hls、平台白名单与 topfunction，并说明它如何被 CI 识别。

lectures.title: 从零编写自己的 L1 内核
lectures.topic: 以 utils 风格为模板，手把手设计一个新 L1 流式内核：模板化头件 + DUT 封装 + test.cpp 测试台 + Makefile/description.json，并跑通 csim/csynth。
learning_goals: 独立设计一个符合规范的 L1 流式内核
编写配套 testbench 与 makefile
跑通 csim 与 csynth 并读懂报告
lectures.practice_task: 实现一个 stream_double（把输入流每元素乘 2 输出）的完整 L1 用例，包含 hpp/test.cpp/Makefile/description.json，并跑通 csim。

lectures.title: 基准评测与对标 CPU/参考
lectures.topic: 讲解各库 benchmarks 目录的组织（blas/solver/security/dsp/vision）、如何与 CPU/参考模型对标（如 dsp host.cpp 的 ref_output 比对与误差阈值），以及性能指标解读。
learning_goals: 理解 benchmarks 目录的组织与用途
掌握与参考模型比对的误差判定方式
学会解读吞吐/延迟性能指标
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 dsp host.cpp 的结果校验段，说明它如何用 ref_output.txt 与误差 level 判定 PASS/FAIL，并讨论为何参考模型不是 bit 精确。

units.title: 集成与部署

lectures.title: 依赖图与跨库组合
lectures.topic: 讲解 dependency.json 表达的跨库依赖（utils←data_mover←dsp←solver 等），如何在同一工程里同时包含多个库的 include 路径，以及 solver 复用 dsp、dsp 复用 utils/data_mover 的实例。
learning_goals: 理解跨库依赖在工程上的体现
掌握多库 include 路径的组织方式
认识 solver↔dsp↔utils 的复用关系
lectures.practice_task: 设计一个同时用到 utils 与 dsp 的工程，写出需要的 -I include 路径列表，并依据 dependency.json 推断若要用 solver 还需额外引入哪些库。

lectures.title: 完整部署：hw 构建、SD 卡与已知问题
lectures.topic: 讲解从 hw_emu 到真实 hw 构建的代价与流程、嵌入式平台的 SD 卡/Common Image/sysroot 依赖、平台重定向（platform_map.json），以及 README 中记录的已知问题与废弃库的处理。
learning_goals: 理解 hw 构建的代价与产出
掌握嵌入式平台 sysroot/Common Image/SD 卡依赖
学会用 platform_map.json 重定向平台并规避已知问题
minimal_modules: 平台重定向与已知问题
lectures.practice_task: 依据 platform_map.json 把 vck190 映射到具体 xpfm，并说明嵌入式 hw 构建需要额外准备 sysroot/Image/rootfs 的原因。
